rules.description: When a line has multiple numbers, values with NT$, $, 元, 圓, or 塊 are stronger price candidates than bare numbers.
A price must be anchored to a billable item, ticket type, plan, venue, rental object, service, or add-on.
Age ranges such as 0 歲, 未滿 1 歲, 2-6 years old, or age labels are not prices.
Route, trip, itinerary, option, and plan indexes are section identifiers, not prices.
Capacity, ml, cc, calories, kcal, grams, seats, or volume numbers are not prices.
Counts, quantity, people, pieces, packs, boxes, hours, days, and duration numbers are not prices unless explicitly marked as charge amounts.
Size columns should become optionGroups.size instead of duplicate base item names.
When taskType is ticket_activity, extracted billable rows should default to category=ticket unless clearly non-ticket.
Topping, upgrade, and add-on lines should not become base items unless explicitly sold standalone.
Free-shipping, minimum-spend, full-order discount, and group-buy threshold amounts are policy numbers, not item prices.
Coupon face values, discount amounts, percent-off values, and buy-one-get-one counts are discount policy values, not item prices.
Service charge, tax, discount, and surcharge percentages are rates and must not be stored as absolute item prices.
Subtotal, grand total, paid amount, and change rows are summary fields and must not become selectable base items.
Receipt numbers, tax IDs, invoice IDs, dates, times, and card last-four values must never enter item price fields.
Deposit, guarantee, reservation, or prepayment amounts must keep an explicit role label instead of silently becoming the full item price.
Check-in, checkout, open, close, session, and departure times are not prices.
Distance, mileage, kilometers, route numbers, and license plate numbers are not prices.
Points, bonus credits, stored-value bonuses, and redemption units must not be mixed with cash prices unless a cash conversion is explicitly stated.
LLM and WebMCP may prepare drafts and suggestions, but final approval and export actions remain human-controlled.
